issues.description: The template header declares the class as 'Image24' while the implementation and constructors are named 'Bitmap24'. This class-name/constructor mismatch in the template will cause compilation errors and prevents students from building or linking the provided example program.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name in the template header match the implementation. Rename 'class Image24' to 'class Bitmap24' in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp (or alternatively rename the implementation/constructors to Image24) so the class name and constructor definitions are consistent.

issues.description: The Bitmap class is declared with two different identifiers across header and implementation: the header declares class Image24 (Bitmap24.hpp) while the implementation defines Bitmap24::Bitmap24 and Bitmap24::~Bitmap24 (Bitmap24.cpp). This naming mismatch makes the same conceptual entity (the 24-bit bitmap image class) appear under different identifiers, causing compilation failures and unnecessary confusion for students mapping the API to its implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the class identifier across header and implementation. Rename the class in Bitmap24.hpp from Image24 to Bitmap24 (or rename the implementation symbols to Image24::...) so that the header declaration and the .cpp definitions use the same class name (Bitmap24) and eliminate the compilation/mapping mismatch.
